issues.title: Definition of hyperbolic space

failure_location.quote: From a geometric point of view, the hyperbolic space is defined as a complete Riemannian manifold with constant curvature $-1$. This abstract definition makes sense, since all the manifolds satisfying the aforementioned properties are isometric.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: the translation in the $x_1$ direction, which is an isometry of $\HH$;

issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims that every complete Riemannian manifold of constant curvature -1 is isometric to every other one. The old metric is invariant under horizontal translations, so quotienting the half-plane by integer horizontal translations gives a complete constant-curvature -1 cylinder that is not isometric to the simply connected half-plane. Thus the old characterization is too broad; for the fixed dimension already active in context, simple connectedness is the material missing condition.
issues.overall_effect: The preliminary uniqueness characterization is false as written, but the subsequent analysis explicitly fixes the half-plane model, so no later formal result is affected.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the characterization by: “For fixed dimension n, hyperbolic space H^n is, up to isometry, the unique complete, simply connected n-dimensional Riemannian manifold of constant sectional curvature -1.” No downstream argument requires alteration because the paper subsequently fixes the half-plane model.
issues.why_classification: The repair is local and requires no proof reconstruction, but it is not a typo or a merely technical qualification: simple connectedness retracts the coherent claim for the natural and substantial class of complete constant-curvature quotients, such as the hyperbolic cylinder. The corrected uniqueness characterization remains recognizably comparable, so the loss is limited rather than major.

new_version_repair_locator.quote: From a geometric point of view, the hyperbolic space is defined as the unique $n$-dimensional, complete, simply connected Riemannian manifold with constant sectional curvature equal to $-1$.

issues.title: Euclidean consistency claim lacks regularity assumptions
issues.failure_explanation: The display claims a uniform O(h^2) consistency estimate on the closed interval [0,T] for a solution whose initial datum is unqualified. At t=0, the expression contains Π_hΔ_eu_0, which is not defined for generic nonsmooth data, and the central-difference Taylor estimate requires controlled fourth spatial derivatives. The old source provides the pointwise Taylor formulas but no uniform L^2 derivative assumption supporting the displayed norm estimate.
issues.overall_effect: This defeats the illustrative Euclidean consistency assertion but does not affect the later hyperbolic results, which use separate regularity hypotheses and consistency proofs.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Qualify the consistency display by assuming that the Euclidean heat solution has uniformly bounded fourth spatial derivatives in L2 on [0,T]; for the homogeneous heat flow, it suffices to assume u0 belongs to H4(R2). Then the central-difference remainder gives the same uniform O(h^2) estimate, including at t=0. No later result needs modification.
issues.why_classification: This is a genuine missing-premise defect rather than a transcription error, but the required smoothness qualification is standard, local, and already indicated by the cited Taylor expansions. It preserves the method, norm, closed time interval, and second-order rate in the intended regular regime, and the assertion has no affected dependents.

issues.title: Second-grid bounded-domain indices

failure_location.quote: \ell_{h,D}^2\coloneqq\left\{(v^h_{i,j})_{i\in Z_1, j\in Z_2} \in \ell_h^2, \rm{with}~Z_1 = \overline{- N, N}\,, Z_2 = \overline{1, M}\right\}\,,

issues.failure_explanation: The second grid has vertical nodes x_2=e^{jh}, while the bounded domain has vertical range [1/D,D]. Restricting j to 1,...,M retains only rows above 1 and omits even j=0, so the declared finite grid does not discretize the lower part of the domain. The corrected range -M,...,M reaches both e^{-Mh}, near 1/D, and e^{Mh}, near D.
issues.overall_effect: The literal finite-grid construction and its interface with the restricted second Laplacian are malformed, so the bounded consistency argument and the fully discrete convergence theorem for the second-grid choice require the corrected reading. The algorithmic membership test and table node counts already indicate the intended symmetric range.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace Z2 = overline{1,M} by Z2 = overline{-M,M} in the definition of the bounded second-grid space, and use that corrected range in the restricted second Laplacian and Theorem thm:convergence-theta. No proof or guarantee otherwise changes.
issues.why_classification: The correction is uniquely forced by the nodes x2=e^{jh}, the vertical domain [1/D,D], the definition of M, the algorithmic membership test, and the table's node counts. The reasoning consistently requires the symmetric range, so the displayed lower endpoint is a transcriptional index error rather than a defect requiring mathematical reconstruction.

issues.title: Tail-control invocation range

failure_location.quote: Further, Lemma \ref{acaret:lem:radius-inside} implies that, if $\x\in \HH\setminus\mathbb{H}^2_{D}$, then $d_g(\mathrm{O},\x)\geq \log(D/2)$.

issues.failure_explanation: The lemma quantifies over every h>0. With D=ζh^{-γ}, this does not imply D>2, yet the cited radius lemma explicitly assumes D>2. Thus that invocation does not establish the proof for D<=2. The missing cases are elementary: when D<=2, d_g(O,x)>=0 gives D<=2<=2e^{d_g(O,x)}; when D>2, the radius lemma applies.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of the all-h tail estimate and consequently the all-h heat-tail corollary is incomplete only for D<=2. The later small-h convergence regime already has D>2.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Split the proof according to D. If D>2, apply the cited radius lemma. If 0<D<=2, use d_g(O,x)>=0 to obtain D<=2<=2e^{d_g(O,x)} for every x. Thus D<=2e^{d_g(O,x)} holds in both cases, after which the existing weighted estimate and the heat-tail corollary proceed unchanged for every h>0.
issues.why_classification: The old proof genuinely invokes a dependency outside its hypothesis, so this is not a typo. Nevertheless, one elementary local case split closes the gap while preserving the all-h quantifier, bound, rate, and dependent heat-tail corollary exactly, with no new lemma or proof architecture.

new_version_repair_locator.quote: Further, using the formula \eqref{eq:hyp-distance} of distance function on $\HH$ we obtain that, if $\x\in \HH\setminus\mathbb{H}^2_{D}$, then $d_g(\mathrm{O},\x)\geq \log(D/2)$.
